landmarks.name: Montpetit Hall
facts: It is the original sports building, next to the Minto Sports Complex.

landmarks.name: Morisset Hall
facts: The university began in 1848 as the College of Bytown, founded by Ottawa's first Catholic bishop.

landmarks.name: Tabaret Hall
facts: Its domed, columned front is the university's best-known image; it houses the central administration.
It was designed by New York architect A. O. Von Herbulis to replace a building lost to fire.

landmarks.name: Advanced Research Complex
facts: A photonics lab can be seen through a two-storey window in its lobby.

landmarks.name: Desmarais Building
facts: It houses the Telfer School of Management.

landmarks.name: Fauteux Hall
facts: It is home to the Faculty of Law.
It was built in 1973 and named after a former Chief Justice of Canada.

landmarks.name: Colonel By Building
facts: It is an engineering building named after the builder of the Rideau Canal.
A green roof was set up on its rooftop in 1971.

landmarks.name: Simard Hall
facts: Café Alt, a green and fair-trade student café, opened in its basement in October 2008.

landmarks.name: Hamelin Hall
facts: It is at 70 Laurier Avenue East and was called Arts Hall until September 2015.
